Lightfield co-founder and CEO Keith Peiris on why AI ends swim lanes and makes everyone a generalist:

"One of the things I regret about Tome that we've definitely fixed with Lightfield is... Henry, my co-founder, says this all the time: We had a lot of people playing house."

"You have the product leader and the marketing leader and the CS leader, and they all have their swim lanes, and they get really mad if someone gives them feedback about something in their swim lane."

"Because of that, we were slowed to a crawl. Maybe put another way, it was impossible to pivot."

"So we're like, none of that. No one has a swim lane. Everyone owns product and everyone owns customer success... We have 40 people at the company. Everyone shows up to the same standup every morning. We stack rank the most important problems... and then whoever's free just takes them."

"Because of the age that we're in... We have this environment where basically everyone is a generalist. Engineers run projects, designers run projects, CSMs run projects."

@keithpeiris @joeschmidtiv

candidates.text:
Here's what I'd teach someone now if they wanted to get into AI implementation 

1. Understand Business Models

Ultimately no one wants AI. They want AI to produce an outcome for them. 

Consumer brands want to buy the right amount of product and sell all of it at a goal efficiency 

Agencies want to sell their employees labor as efficiently as possible

etc 

Understand the business model so you can sell the outcome of your work

2. Low Hanging Fruit

So much impact can be made by just enabling internal usage of Claude Code or Codex. 

Don't chase the fancy agents in the beginning.  

3. Senior Executive Buy In Is Almost All That Matters (Preferably the CEO)

Ideally you want the CEO as your primary POC. 

AI is about change. Low level employees can't produce change. They don't have the confidence or permission to do so. Most of the time they'll BLOCK you. 

You need to work with the most senior person possible. 

4. Context Context Context

First connect systems, connectors are free context. Next create a file-system brain. Next make it frictionless for a new user to use it and stay in sync. Next build automations. 

5. Protect Yourself Against Scope Creep or Blocking 

Charge hourly or monthly retainer. Have contractual agreements in place if your client does not provide the context or access you need to work. Make sure they know about front what they are committing to and what is involved. 

I made this mistake so many times, and it cost me so much money.

what mike describes happened to almost every industry where information arbitrage was leverage (which was a ton).

first the internet compressed the value of knowing something others didn’t then pushed the remaining edge into smaller & smaller windows of time. e.g. in high frequency trading milliseconds of informational advantage can still be worth enormous amounts. even trump is monetizing earlier access to truth social posts to the tune of $100k +. second the same thing also happened to ordinary life (pick your category) in so many ways (see lines forming in nyc as a very basic example).

in essence the internet killed info scarcity. & ai is now coming for the scarcity of interpretation of that info too. that will be even more transformative.
